On 29.01.2024, Petitions No. 235/MP/2023 and 192/MP/2021 were taken up together before the Commission. During the hearing, proxy counsel for TPDDL sought a short adjournment on the grounds that the arguing counsel was unavailable on that date, and the other parties did not oppose this request. The Commission acceded to the request and adjourned both matters for further hearing on 03.04.2024. On 02.04.2025, SBSR requested that, given the nature of the issues involved, the matters be taken up in a physical hearing mode, a request not opposed by the Respondents. On 30.04.2025, the matter was part-heard and again listed for hearing on 07.07.2025, at which the matter was reserved for order. The Commission also permitted the parties to file their respective written submissions, if any, within two weeks. - b) As already demonstrated above and in the present application, there have been subsequent developments, on account of the stand taken subsequently by SECI, which are required to be brought to the notice of this Commission for the purpose of deciding the real controversy involved in the present case. Therefore, the Commission should exercise its discretionary powers to allow the amendment in the present petition. _**Project and the beneficiaries TPDDL and BYPL to submit on affidavit by 17.5.2023 that they would bear additional financial implications, if any due to “Change in Law” as per PPA and PSA as per decision of the commission, with an advance copy to the other parties** . The Commission also directed the Petitioner to make its submissions on affidavit by 17.5.2023 with a copy to the other parties._ - n) Further, the Respondents (TPDDL and BYPL) have adopted the said view time and again. This is evident from the minutes of the meetings dated 26.08.2022 and 31.01.2023, wherein the Buying Entities categorically stated that they are willing to offtake 62.4 MW of power without any financial implications, including effects of change in law. This position of Discom was, however, interpreted entirely in a different manner by the said Discoms during the course of proceedings of the present petition held on 02.05.2023, by stating that the statement that they will not bear any additional financial implication as captured under MoM was meant for claims other than a change in law in terms of the PPA. This clearly shows that the Respondent Discoms are also trying to approbate and reprobate by changing their stand, which cannot be allowed above concession, it is submitted that it is a settled tenet of law that a concession of fact by a party is binding upon the said party. - p) Thus, once the amendment of the petition and reliefs is allowed by this Commission, the rights of parties are sub-judice in terms of the subject matter of the dispute. After the allowance of amendment, the subject matter in Petition No. 192/MP/2021 is no longer concerned with the power supply of the uncommissioned capacity of 150 MW ( _i.e., capacity left after the long stop date_ ). ## _**Re: The present Petition is not maintainable in view of the concession of TPDDL in the Order dated 12.12.2022, which puts a bar upon TPDDL from asking the relief of supply of Subject Capacity.**_ - s) SBSR is attempting to approbate and reprobate its stand upon the subject issue in the present Petition.
